data.long_meaning: Sarangdevi is a female deity in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted as a goddess of love, beauty, and music. She is also known as the 'Lady of the Sarang Tree', and is believed to reside in the heart chakra, providing emotional balance and inner peace. The name Sarangdevi carries the meaning “Lady of the Sarang Tree” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sarangdevi usually hope their child will grow to embody lady of the sarang tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Sarangdevi was an important deity in the ancient Hindu city of Pratisthal (Prayagraj), located in modern-day Uttar Pradesh, India. She was revered as the goddess of fertility and was believed to protect pregnant women and childbirth. Sarangdevi is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Puranas and the Agni Purana.

Another reference to Sarangdevi can be found in the Mahabharata, where she is described as the mother of the Pandava hero Bhima. According to the epic, Sarangdevi was a forest goddess who protected the forest and its inhabitants. When Bhima was born, she took him under her protection and raised him, teaching him various skills and martial arts.

modern_usage.modern_context: Sarangdevi, also known as Saraswati, is a popular Hindu deity revered as the Goddess of Love and Marriage, as well as the Mother Goddess and Nature Goddess. In Hindu mythology, she is often depicted as a beautiful and graceful woman with multiple arms, holding various symbols like a veena, a lotus flower, or a mala. Sarangdevi is particularly worshipped during weddings and marriage ceremonies, where she is believed to bless the newlyweds with a long and harmonious marital life. Her worship extends beyond Hindu mythology and is also found in various forms of art and culture, such as paintings, sculptures, and music. In modern times, Sarangdevi continues to be an important figure in Indian weddings and marriage rituals, and her iconography and symbolism are often incorporated into wedding decorations and attire.
